### Step 5 — Verify

The unit is the criterion (`5/<AC-id>`): its Test design row, its state the run's log's (`reader.sh <plan> cell <AC>`). Step 5 owes each criterion's evidence, the walk, the auditor and the regression.

**The walk opens verification.** Before any row discharges, an agent that has NOT read the acceptance criteria spends about fifteen minutes using the shipped plugin as a user would — on a tiny plan, through a dispatch and a landing — and narrates what it sees at the code and behavior this wave intentionally changed: what was seen, never whether an expectation was met.

The narration goes to `<docs-root>/record/`, registered with `session-poker.sh proof-add walk <record>`: the run's newest walk proof is the walk the gate reads, any spelling must land under `record/`, and a `..` component is refused outright. **The artifact carries zero AC identifiers unless it is a registered walk**, a verdict table `proof-add walk` parsed, whose identifiers are its verdicts: a narration that says "AC-4: confirmed" is a checklist wearing prose. Existence is the wall the gate can check, from step 5 through 9; running it first is discipline no hook can see.

**The regression, once.** A build row runs the suites its brief names. After the last build row lands, one whole run at that head when the plan's `regression:` is `yes`, one verdict per suite; `regression-run` refuses it at `regression: no`, beside an open build row, at a head that already has a whole run, or at a head the full pass's state reads green by content. A red suite is a fix row's: record the run (proof-add regression <log>, the line regression-run prints), then add the row with --born regression:<suite>; the marker reads the run's red. A whole run at a later head where code landed is the normal path. A head whose landings since the pass moved no code reads green and needs none. The regression is one whole run at a commit F on the branch plus the greens of what changed: a suite red in F is owed until one later green of it; every later commit is proved by the suites its row ran. Close reads it again from the branch's ref. At `regression: no`, the person's header key, no run is owed. The plan names the regression, every applicable suite and the build; the orchestrator runs it (`session-poker.sh regression-run` for a declared `regression-command:`, else any command whose log opens `head=<40-hex> dirty=0` and ends `rc=0`) and cites the logs with `session-poker.sh proof-add regression <log>…`. A run at an ancestor of the working head still proves it when every later commit on the branch is proved by the runs recorded at it; otherwise `proof-add regression` names the first commit it cannot prove and the suites it lacks there.

**The run outlives the session.** A suite call the wall wraps runs detached, and its caller waits on that call; `stop-run <name|run id> --why '<reason>'` stops it, and a run whose process is gone with no end written is `LOST` (exit 70), never green.

**Environments — declared, covered, fog.** A plan's frontmatter may carry `environments:`, one line of entries joined by " · ", each `<name> (covered by this wave)` or `<name> (fog — cure: <how it gets covered instead>)`. A fog environment is one the plan names but this run cannot execute on. Naming the set is optional. Naming it binds: the walk's proof names every declared non-fog environment (`proof-add walk <record> --environments <names>`), and a fog entry with no cure blocks. This is a claim about *where* the regression ran, never a substitute for it.

"Every applicable suite" is a **discovered** set, not whatever the default command runs. Check `package.json`, `Makefile`, CI config, test-runner configs, and test directories for suites the default runner omits — a hand-listed runner that silently drops a suite reports green over untested code. When a change touches code with existing tests, triage each affected test as UPDATE / ADD / REMOVE / OK before implementing, not after.

**A criterion is discharged by an event, never by an edit:** the walk proof that confirms it, the user's `approve <AC> '<their words>'` at T4, or their `waive <AC> '<their words>'`. Its tier is its Test design row's, changed only by editing that row.

**The T0–T4 ladder.** Each tier is defined by which lie it makes impossible.

| Tier | Name | Proves | The false green it kills |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T0** | Static | compiles / builds / lints | type & build breaks |
| **T1** | Unit | logic at mocked seams | wrong logic |
| **T2** | Hermetic | real browser + real engine over a **declared-fidelity fixture** | integration breaks — *only if the fixture matches the real data shape* |
| **T3** | Live agent-drive | the **declared real surface**, real data, cold client, trusted input, feature-scoped semantic readback | every proxy: wrong surface, stale artifact, synthetic data, warm caches |
| **T4** | Human walk | the user's own hands and eyes | perceptual / judgment gaps automation can't close |

A lower tier passing while a higher one fails is a **locator, not a contradiction** — the bug lives in exactly the layer the lower tier elides.

**Required evidence.** Every criterion owes evidence, a real file under `record/` its proof names; a T4 criterion also owes the user's approval naming it.

**Tier-Discharge Rule.** Lower-tier evidence never discharges a higher-tier row; higher-tier evidence discharges lower-tier rows for the same AC. A row whose criterion names a PRODUCER and a CONSUMER (a library function AND the hook that calls it; a value AND the surface that renders it) is discharged only by evidence that reaches the consumer — the producer's own suite green is the lower tier of that row, not the row. A green suite can never stand in for a T3 row. T3's validity conditions live in `browser-verify`; do not restate them. An undrivable T3 row is **blocked**, loudly, never silently skipped. T4 rows are discharged by the user's `approve <AC> '<what they walked>'` — agents never self-confirm one. The browser modality's `playwright-cli` is an environment-class dependency: `jit_check` detects absence, `jit_offer` (`payload/scripts/lib/jit.sh`) offers the install, and a decline degrades cleanly per its printed line, never a row silently unattempted.

**Absence-readback rule.** A readback that is zero, empty, or not-present proves nothing on its own — an all-zero observation reads identically whether the code works or was deleted. Such a row needs a paired positive case: the same readback returning a non-empty result where the behavior says it should. Without one the row is presumed powerless and cannot discharge, at any tier.

**False-green rule.** On finding any test that passed over broken code, the gate cannot close until a record names `false-green: <test — what it lied about>` AND a paired `rewritten: <ref>` proving the test now goes RED.

**Vocabulary.** Say "delivered/fixed/verified" only at the row's contracted tier. Below tier the honest phrasing is "implemented, verification pending."

**Mid-discharge commits.** At step 5, rows still pending are exempt from their evidence and the auditor is owed only once none remain. The full contract bites on the 5→6 advance, and the criteria are judged again at every step from 6 on. Advance with `session-poker.sh current 6`: it dry-runs every wall and appends nothing on a refusal. **Never take the step back to dodge a gate.**

#### Auditor — the Step-5 exit gate

A **fresh, independent** exec-complex agent (`subagent_type: bionic:auditor`) — never the implementer, never a fork of the orchestrator, whose context is the thing under audit. At `double` it holds `evidence`; its brief names `Questions: evidence` and nothing of the checks, which `payload/context/checks-evidence.md` delivers to it at start. At `single` the critic holds `evidence` with its other questions.

**The whole read, once.** When the code settles — the last build row landed — dispatch the reviewers the rigor deals, the critic and at `double` the auditor, in one batch on that head, each with `scope: whole` and one record per question it is dealt, every record listed on its brief's `Files:` line and `Expected artifact:` naming one; none waits for another's verdict. A fix after it is read as `steps/6.md` says.

Bounds: audits the verification, not the wave — never re-verifies the feature, re-runs the whole suite, or reviews the code. One auditor per read.

Row verdicts and the wave verdict, `auditor-wave: <verdict> — <coverage finding>`, are written in its record, which the orchestrator registers with `proof-add review` (`steps/6.md`). Any REFUTED or UNVERIFIABLE row blocks closure absent a waiver, and so does a non-CONFIRMED wave verdict — which is where a requirement with no row can be reported at all.

#### Waiver Protocol

Three moves are the user's, never an agent's: a tier **downgrade**, an **`n/a` on a live tier (T3/T4)**, and **closing over a non-CONFIRMED row**. Each is the user's `waive <AC> '<their words>' '<why>'`, one waiver event. A waived row is exempt from its evidence and from CONFIRMED. Agents never self-write `n/a` on a live-tier field.

**A user-confirmed T4 row is none of those moves, and needs no waiver.** T4's evidence *is* the user's confirmation, so an auditor sent at it can only re-read what the user said — transcription, not independence. A T4 row the user's approval names therefore discharges past the Verify gate on that alone, with no auditor verdict and no waiver. The attribution is the whole test: an unattributed or agent-written claim ("confirmed after the re-render") is not a user confirmation and still meets the CONFIRMED wall.

Note the hole: retyping a criterion's tier from T3 to T2 in its Test design row is a downgrade no hook sees.

**Design waiver.** A fourth user-only move, sitting on the artifact rather than on a matrix row: `design-waived: <user> <date> <reason>` in a wave-or-epic spec's frontmatter, quieting the design wall for that artifact. Recorded, not validated — presence is the whole check, matching the `rigor-override:` precedent, and the fields are written for the next reader. An agent never writes one.
